cases.answer: Among adults with type 2 diabetes, the intention-to-treat comparison favored digital DSMES+CGM over usual care at both time points, but was statistically significant only at three months. At three months, HbA1c was 0.7 percentage points lower (95% CI −1.4 to −0.1; P=.03), equivalent to −8.1 mmol/mol (95% CI −15.5 to −0.7). At six months, the difference was slightly smaller and nonsignificant: −0.6 percentage points (95% CI −1.4 to 0.2; P=.12), equivalent to −6.9 mmol/mol (95% CI −15.7 to 1.9).

claims.claim: The trial compared digital DSMES+CGM with usual care in adults with type 2 diabetes.
claims.quote:
Methods: Participants with type 2 diabetes and HbA 1c of 8% or higher (64 mmol/mol) who were not using mealtime bolus
insulin (aged 26 ‐83 y; mean HbA 1c 9.6%, SD 1.4% [mean 81.2 mmol/mol, SD 15.8 mmol/mol]) were randomly assigned to
a digital DSMES+CGM integrated solution (n=51) or usual care (n=49) for 6 months.

claims.claim: The main intention-to-treat HbA1c comparison was significant at three months but not at six months.

cases.ambiguity: If the question refers to the sensitivity analysis excluding participants who never participated in the intervention, both comparisons were significant: −1.0 percentage point at three months (95% CI −1.6 to −0.3; P=.01) and −0.8 percentage points at six months (95% CI −1.6 to −0.02; P=.046).
